questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How spending time in nature can help mental health
How to grow plants in a city garden
The tallest trees in the world
Why medicine is the best treatment for depression
questions.why: Neil and Georgina discuss ecotherapy, which uses contact with nature to help people.

questions.q: What does Georgina usually do to cheer herself up?
options: Have a drink with friends at the local pub
Do some gardening in her back garden
Go for a walk, especially in the countryside
Hug a tree in the park near her office
questions.why: She says having a walk usually helps, especially in the countryside.

questions.q: According to the charity Mind, what is ecotherapy?
options: A type of medication made from plants and herbs
A formal treatment with outdoor activities in nature
A relaxing holiday in the countryside with friends
A way to study wild animals in their natural habitat
questions.why: Mind describes it as a formal treatment which involves doing outdoor activities in nature.

questions.q: What does Patricia Hasbach think about ecotherapy?
options: It can cure any kind of pain
It should replace traditional therapy
It only works for people who live in cities
It is a useful tool but won't solve everything
questions.why: She calls it 'another tool in the therapist's toolbox' but 'not a panacea'.

questions.q: What does Patricia Hasbach mean when she says therapy 'stopped at the urban boundary'?
options: Therapists refused to travel and work in the countryside
Therapy was traditionally done indoors in towns and cities
Therapy was far too expensive for people outside cities
City people didn't think they needed therapy at all
questions.why: Georgina explains that going beyond the 'urban boundary' into nature gives another method.

questions.q: According to research, why does nature help us relax?
options: Our brains get a break from always being on guard
The air in the countryside contains more oxygen
We sleep better at night after exercising outdoors
There are fewer people around that we have to talk to
questions.why: Neil says our busy brains are always on guard, but in nature they get a break.

questions.q: According to Birgitta Gatersleben, what happens when we are exposed to nature?
options: We become more tired and want to go home and sleep
We quickly start to miss the noise and energy of city life
We feel more energetic, but also more stressed and alert
Negative feelings are quickly replaced by positive ones
questions.why: She says our negative feelings get almost immediately replaced with positive emotions.

questions.q: What does 'biophilia' suggest about most people?
options: They must slowly learn to enjoy nature as children
They prefer the company of animals to other people
They are born with a natural connection to nature
They are naturally afraid of wild and empty places
questions.why: Georgina says most of us were born to connect with nature.
